idiom_name: typed request augmentation: Express.User merged with the descriptor shape
implementation_notes: The pattern shows up as a typing problem: the descriptor is the object the authentication middleware attaches to the request, and the value is making its shape visible to the compiler. @types/passport declares an empty global Express.User interface and augments Express.Request with user?: User plus isAuthenticated(), so the application declares the descriptor once with declaration merging and every handler reads req.user.roles with checking. Framework-agnostic or serverless code should skip the global augmentation and thread an explicit Principal type (or a per-request context object); the classic authenticator/factory structure is replaced by one middleware and one declared type.
pitfalls: Express.User is an empty global interface by default and declaration merging is module-global: two packages augmenting it conflict, and adding required members breaks code that only saw the empty type.
req.user is typed User | undefined: non-null assertions and casts erase exactly the check the augmentation bought, so narrow it once in a guard.
A decoded (not verified) JWT produces a descriptor-shaped object that TypeScript happily accepts - the type cannot express "verified", so only the middleware may construct User.
